entries.name: cases … with | ctor
entries.notes: DECIDED (editor). §E books this shape at unit 19 (22-exec) as inversion on a derivation, but the same syntax splits a VALUE of an inductive type, which is legal from unit 02 (03-compute) — corpus `star_forall_right_fails` does `cases x with | false | true` on a `Bool` at 17-star-algebra.lean:69. A regex cannot tell a value split from a derivation inversion, so the row is booked at the EARLIEST legal form, as `cases` itself already is. entries.name: cases on a value or a constructor-equality hypothesis
entries.notes: MISSING FROM §E.1, added by editorial decision. §E.1 gives `cases` three rows — saved-equation at unit 02, inversion and `with | ctor` at unit 20 — and none of them covers two forms the course actually uses at unit 02: `cases h` where `h : some v = none` (a constructor equality), and `cases x with | false | true` on a value of an inductive type. VERIFIED BEFORE ENCODING: §D unit 02’s exercise x08 prescribes `intro h; cases h` verbatim, so this is the plan contradicting its own ledger, not an author freelancing; and no fragment before 03-compute uses `cases` in any form (02-terms uses `rcases`, which has its own row). Booked at file 03-compute = §E unit 02. Mind the offset: unit 02 is NOT 02-terms. `check: false` because the `cases` token row and the `cases … with | ctor` shape row do the matching; this row exists so the ledger states the rule and §tactics can print it.

entries.name: theorem
entries.notes: CORE SYNTAX IS TRACKED BY SHAPE, NOT BY NAME. `fun` and `by` have no rows of their own: they are covered by the shape rows `fun x => e` and `:= by`, whose `re` field matches the construct in context. That is deliberate — a bare `by` is not a citation of anything, and a row per keyword would fire on every proof in the course. --sweep knows about `re` rows and will not re-report them. Raised by 02-terms’ author, who observed the asymmetry with this row; recorded here so it is not re-litigated.
